description: Create the useVoiceToText hook and integrate it into the ReportIssue page. This feature is independent of FEAT-001 — both touch different files and can be verified independently.
steps: Create frontend/src/hooks/useVoiceToText.js. The hook must: (a) detect SpeechRecognition via `window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition`; (b) accept a `lang` param defaulting to 'hi-IN'; (c) return `{ isListening, transcript, start, stop, supported }`; (d) on start(), reset transcript to '' then begin recognition with `interimResults: true` and `lang` set; (e) accumulate results in state by concatenating `event.results[i].transcript` for all result items; (f) on stop(), call recognition.stop(); (g) set isListening true on start, false on end/error; (h) clean up recognition on unmount. Export as default named export `useVoiceToText`.

Integrate into frontend/src/pages/Citizen/ReportIssue.jsx: (a) import `useVoiceToText` from '../../hooks/useVoiceToText'; import `Mic`, `MicOff`, `Globe` from 'lucide-react' (add to existing lucide import line). (b) Add state: `const [voiceLang, setVoiceLang] = useState('hi-IN');`. (c) Call hook: `const { isListening, transcript, start: startVoice, stop: stopVoice, supported: voiceSupported } = useVoiceToText(voiceLang);`. (d) Add useEffect that appends transcript to the description field: when `transcript` changes and is non-empty, call `setFormData(prev => ({ ...prev, description: prev.description ? prev.description + ' ' + transcript : transcript }))`. (e) Locate the description textarea block (~line 244–254 of the file). Directly below the `</textarea>` closing tag, insert the voice controls: a wrapping `<div className='mt-2 flex items-center gap-2'>` containing: a language selector `<select>` with options hi-IN/mr-IN/en-US that sets `voiceLang` (only show if `voiceSupported`); a mic toggle button that calls `isListening ? stopVoice() : startVoice()` with a pulsing red dot when `isListening` (use `animate-pulse` on a red circle) and `Mic`/`MicOff` icon; hide the entire block if `!voiceSupported`. The button text: 'Stop' when listening, 'Voice Input' when not.
Do NOT add any new npm dependencies — SpeechRecognition is a browser native API.
acceptance_criteria: frontend/src/hooks/useVoiceToText.js exists and exports a default function.
ReportIssue.jsx imports the hook and renders the mic button + language selector in the description section.
If the browser supports SpeechRecognition the mic button is visible; if not, it is hidden.
Clicking the mic button toggles isListening; spoken words are appended (not replaced) to the description textarea.
`cd frontend && npm run build` completes with no errors after the changes.
verification: Run `cd frontend && npm run build` — must complete with 0 errors.

In a Chromium browser (SpeechRecognition is supported), open ReportIssue page: verify mic button is visible, clicking it starts recognition, spoken text appears in the description textarea appended to any existing text.
In a browser without SpeechRecognition (or disable the API): verify the mic button is not rendered.
findings: Hook created at frontend/src/hooks/useVoiceToText.js using browser-native SpeechRecognition. Integrated into ReportIssue.jsx: voiceLang state (default hi-IN), hook call, useEffect that appends transcript to description, and voice controls block (Globe icon + language selector + mic toggle button with pulsing red dot) rendered below the textarea, hidden when voiceSupported is false. Build passes with 0 errors.
